segments: Through all these the ambassadors passed,
and they brought them out into a spacious garden,
in which there was a pool of water
made of white lead, which was indistinguishable from silver.
And above the pool was a great tree forged from silver,
and most of its branches and leaves were gilded,
which swayed with the gentle breeze that blew.
And upon them were birds of gold and silver,
which flew by means of cords beneath the ground,
and uttered and made diverse sounds.
And in that same garden were a great many date palms,
plated with sheets of boxwood up to the place of their fronds,
and likewise a great many citron trees bearing fruit.
And from the garden they brought them into a spacious hall,
whose walls were covered with magnificent tapestries,
and upon them were hung ten thousand shields,
and likewise bucklers, bows, and lances.
It is said
that the number of curtains on the walls amounted to twenty-two thousand,
apart from the carpets on the floor that were trodden upon.
And from there they entered a long passage,
in which a thousand white eunuchs bearing weapons were lined up on one side,
and a thousand black eunuchs likewise armed on the other side.
And when they entered the gate,
they saw the Proximus, that is to say the vizier, seated on a high throne,
with legal officers and nobles standing around him;
and the ambassadors supposed that he was the king.
And it was said to them,
"He is the vizier."
And from the presence of the vizier they entered where the king was,
seated on an ebony throne in the form of a dome,
and on one of the corners of the throne were nine rows of sparkling precious stones,
and on the other corner nine.
And his five sons were around him,
three on the right,
and two on the left.
It is said
that the ambassadors sat and rested seven times
before they reached the king.
And when the ambassadors entered,
they gave greeting with their heads alone.
And they said to the interpreter,
"It is fitting for us to kiss the ground,
but lest your ambassador also be required to do so by the kingdom of the Romans,
we have not kissed it.
We make this known
lest you accuse us of ill manners."
